lesson_scope: Non-linear Cartesian complex equations, systems with modulus |z| and conjugate product zz*, fraction conditions with purely real/imaginary values, complex quadratic equations, and higher polynomial roots in Cartesian form.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Solving complex equation with linear z and squared modulus |z|^2.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Substituting z = x + iy and |z|^2 = x^2 + y^2 into non-linear equation.

hints: Substitute $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$ and $|z|^2 = x^2 + y^2$ into $2z + |z|^2 = 15 + 8\mathrm{i}$.
Equate real parts: $2x + x^2 + 4^2 = 15 \implies x^2 + 2x + 1 = 0 \implies x = -1$, giving $z = -1 + 4\mathrm{i}$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$ and $|z|^2 = x^2 + y^2$:
$$2(x + \mathrm{i}y) + (x^2 + y^2) = 15 + 8\mathrm{i}$$
$$(x^2 + y^2 + 2x) + 2\mathrm{i}y = 15 + 8\mathrm{i}$$

Equate imaginary parts:
$$2y = 8 \implies y = 4$$

Equate real parts and substitute $y = 4$:
$$x^2 + 4^2 + 2x = 15 \implies x^2 + 2x + 16 = 15$$
$$x^2 + 2x + 1 = 0 \implies (x + 1)^2 = 0 \implies x = -1$$
Conclusion: $z = -1 + 4\mathrm{i}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$ and $|z|^2 = x^2 + y^2$, and equates imaginary parts to find $y = 4$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Setting imaginary part of rational quotient to zero to find line relation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Deriving linear Cartesian condition for purely real complex fraction.

hints: Set the imaginary part $-xy + (y + 3)(x - 3) = 0$ to get $3x - 3y - 9 = 0 \implies y = x - 3$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$ and multiply by the conjugate of the denominator:
$$\frac{z + 3\mathrm{i}}{z - 3} = \frac{x + \mathrm{i}(y + 3)}{(x - 3) + \mathrm{i}y} = \frac{[x + \mathrm{i}(y + 3)][(x - 3) - \mathrm{i}y]}{(x - 3)^2 + y^2}$$

Extract the imaginary part of the numerator:
$$\operatorname{Im}(\text{Numerator}) = -xy + (y + 3)(x - 3) = -xy + xy - 3y + 3x - 9 = 3x - 3y - 9$$

Set the imaginary part to zero for the fraction to be purely real:
$$3x - 3y - 9 = 0 \implies x - y = 3 \implies y = x - 3$$

ai_rubric.observable: Multiplies by conjugate $(x - 3) - \mathrm{i}y$ and extracts imaginary part $-xy + (y + 3)(x - 3)$.
Sets imaginary part to zero and simplifies to $y = x - 3$ (or $x - y = 3$).

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Finding Cartesian square roots of a complex number.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding square roots of complex numbers with Cartesian quadratic system.

walkthrough.text:
Equate real and imaginary parts of $(x + \mathrm{i}y)^2 = -7 + 24\mathrm{i}$:
$$x^2 - y^2 = -7$$
$$2xy = 24 \implies y = \frac{12}{x}$$

Substitute $y = \frac{12}{x}$ into the first equation:
$$x^2 - \frac{144}{x^2} = -7 \implies x^4 + 7x^2 - 144 = 0$$
$$(x^2 + 16)(x^2 - 9) = 0 \implies x^2 = 9 \implies x = \pm 3$$

Calculate $y$ for each value of $x$:
- For $x = 3$: $y = 4 \implies z = 3 + 4\mathrm{i}$
- For $x = -3$: $y = -4 \implies z = -3 - 4\mathrm{i}$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates $x^2 - y^2 = -7$ and $2xy = 24$, forming and solving quadratic in $x^2$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Solving complex equation with zz* and -3iz.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Cartesian solution of equation involving zz* and linear complex term.

hints: Substitute $x = -3$ into real equation $(-3)^2 + y^2 + 3y = 13 \implies y^2 + 3y - 4 = 0$, and solve for $y = 1, -4$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$ into $z z^* - 3\mathrm{i}z = 13 + 9\mathrm{i}$:
$$(x^2 + y^2) - 3\mathrm{i}(x + \mathrm{i}y) = (x^2 + y^2 + 3y) - 3\mathrm{i}x = 13 + 9\mathrm{i}$$

Equate imaginary parts:
$$-3x = 9 \implies x = -3$$

Substitute $x = -3$ into the real part equation:
$$(-3)^2 + y^2 + 3y = 13 \implies 9 + y^2 + 3y = 13$$
$$y^2 + 3y - 4 = 0 \implies (y + 4)(y - 1) = 0 \implies y = 1 \quad \text{or} \quad y = -4$$
Solutions: $z = -3 + \mathrm{i}$ and $z = -3 - 4\mathrm{i}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$ and $z z^* = x^2 + y^2$, and equates imaginary parts to find $x = -3$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Solving complex fraction equation with zz*.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Removing fraction and grouping real and imaginary parts to solve for z.

hints: Equate imaginary parts to zero: $x + 2y - 8 = 0 \implies x = 8 - 2y$.
Substitute $x = 8 - 2y$ into the real part to get $5y^2 - 27y + 28 = 0$, giving $y = 4$ ($z = 4\mathrm{i}$) and $y = 7/5$ ($z = \frac{26}{5} + \frac{7}{5}\mathrm{i}$).

walkthrough.text:
Rationalise $\frac{5z}{2 - \mathrm{i}}$:
$$\frac{5(x + \mathrm{i}y)(2 + \mathrm{i})}{5} = (2x - y) + \mathrm{i}(x + 2y)$$

Substitute into the equation and separate components:
$$[(2x - y - x^2 - y^2 + 20)] + \mathrm{i}(x + 2y - 8) = 0$$
$$\text{Imaginary part: } x + 2y - 8 = 0 \implies x = 8 - 2y$$

Substitute $x = 8 - 2y$ into the real part equation:
$$2(8 - 2y) - y - [(8 - 2y)^2 + y^2] + 20 = 0$$
$$5y^2 - 27y + 28 = 0 \implies (y - 4)(5y - 7) = 0$$
Solutions: $z = 4\mathrm{i}$ and $z = \frac{26}{5} + \frac{7}{5}\mathrm{i}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Rationalises $\frac{5z}{2 - \mathrm{i}} = (2x - y) + \mathrm{i}(x + 2y)$ and equates imaginary parts to get $x = 8 - 2y$.
Substitutes $x = 8 - 2y$ into real part equation to get $5y^2 - 27y + 28 = 0$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Real ratio line condition combined with modulus circle.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Simultaneous solution of line from fraction condition and circle from modulus.

hints: Rationalise $\frac{x + \mathrm{i}(y + 5)}{(x - 5) + \mathrm{i}y}$ to get imaginary numerator $5x - 5y - 25 = 0 \implies x = y + 5$.
Substitute $x = y + 5$ into $x^2 + y^2 = 17$ to get $2y^2 + 10y + 8 = 0 \implies y^2 + 5y + 4 = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Extract the imaginary part of $\frac{z + 5\mathrm{i}}{z - 5}$:
$$\operatorname{Im}(\text{Numerator}) = -xy + (y + 5)(x - 5) = 5x - 5y - 25 = 0 \implies x = y + 5$$

Substitute $x = y + 5$ into $|z|^2 = x^2 + y^2 = 17$:
$$(y + 5)^2 + y^2 = 17 \implies 2y^2 + 10y + 8 = 0 \implies y^2 + 5y + 4 = 0$$
$$(y + 1)(y + 4) = 0 \implies y = -1 \quad \text{or} \quad y = -4$$

Determine the corresponding $x$ coordinates:
- For $y = -1$: $x = 4 \implies z = 4 - \mathrm{i}$
- For $y = -4$: $x = 1 \implies z = 1 - 4\mathrm{i}$

ai_rubric.observable: Multiplies by $(x - 5) - \mathrm{i}y$ and sets imaginary part $5x - 5y - 25 = 0$ to get $x - y = 5$.
Substitutes $x = y + 5$ into $x^2 + y^2 = 17$ to form $y^2 + 5y + 4 = 0$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Real fraction condition and modulus circle intersection.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Deriving linear relation from purely real fraction.

hints: Multiply numerator and denominator of $\frac{(x + 4) + \mathrm{i}y}{x + \mathrm{i}(y + 4)}$ by $x - \mathrm{i}(y + 4)$.

walkthrough.text:
Multiply by the conjugate of the denominator:
$$\frac{z + 4}{z + 4\mathrm{i}} = \frac{[(x + 4) + \mathrm{i}y][x - \mathrm{i}(y + 4)]}{x^2 + (y + 4)^2}$$

Extract and set the imaginary part of the numerator to zero:
$$\operatorname{Im}(\text{Numerator}) = -(x + 4)(y + 4) + xy = -xy - 4x - 4y - 16 + xy = -4x - 4y - 16 = 0$$
$$x + y = -4$$

ai_rubric.observable: Multiplies by conjugate and sets imaginary part $-(x + 4)(y + 4) + xy = 0$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Intersecting line with circle to find complex solutions.

walkthrough.text:
Solve for $x$:
$$(x + 1)(x + 3) = 0 \implies x = -1 \quad \text{or} \quad x = -3$$

Find corresponding $y$ values:
- For $x = -1$: $y = -(-1) - 4 = -3 \implies z = -1 - 3\mathrm{i}$
- For $x = -3$: $y = -(-3) - 4 = -1 \implies z = -3 - \mathrm{i}$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Forming Cartesian system from quadratic and conjugate terms.

hints: Group real terms $x^2 - y^2 + 2x$ and imaginary terms $2xy - 2y = 2y(x - 1)$.
Set both to zero to obtain the required equations.

walkthrough.text:
Expand $z^2$ and $2z^*$ in Cartesian form:
$$z^2 = (x + \mathrm{i}y)^2 = x^2 - y^2 + 2\mathrm{i}xy$$
$$2z^* = 2(x - \mathrm{i}y) = 2x - 2\mathrm{i}y$$

Group into real and imaginary parts:
$$z^2 + 2z^* = (x^2 - y^2 + 2x) + \mathrm{i}(2xy - 2y) = 0$$
$$\text{Real: } x^2 - y^2 + 2x = 0$$
$$\text{Imaginary: } 2y(x - 1) = 0$$

ai_rubric.observable: Equates to zero to obtain $x^2 - y^2 + 2x = 0$ and $2y(x - 1) = 0$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Deducing non-real roots from Cartesian simultaneous system.

walkthrough.text:
Use the condition $y \neq 0$:
$$2y(x - 1) = 0 \implies x - 1 = 0 \implies x = 1$$

Substitute $x = 1$ into the real part equation:
$$1^2 - y^2 + 2(1) = 0 \implies 3 - y^2 = 0 \implies y^2 = 3 \implies y = \pm\sqrt{3}$$

State the non-real complex solutions:
$$z = 1 + \sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i} \quad \text{and} \quad z = 1 - \sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Solving quadratic equation with complex coefficients via discriminant.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Calculating discriminant of quadratic equation with complex coefficients.

walkthrough.text: Identify coefficients: $a = 2 + \mathrm{i}, b = 4, c = 2 - \mathrm{i}$.

Evaluate the product $4ac$:
$$4ac = 4(2 + \mathrm{i})(2 - \mathrm{i}) = 4(2^2 + 1^2) = 4(5) = 20$$

Compute the discriminant:
$$\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = 16 - 20 = -4$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Evaluating roots via quadratic formula and conjugate rationalisation.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the quadratic formula with $\sqrt{\Delta} = \pm 2\mathrm{i}$:
$$w = \frac{-4 \pm 2\mathrm{i}}{2(2 + \mathrm{i})} = \frac{-2 \pm \mathrm{i}}{2 + \mathrm{i}}$$

Evaluate the first root:
$$w_1 = \frac{(-2 + \mathrm{i})(2 - \mathrm{i})}{(2 + \mathrm{i})(2 - \mathrm{i})} = \frac{-4 + 2\mathrm{i} + 2\mathrm{i} - \mathrm{i}^2}{5} = \frac{-3 + 4\mathrm{i}}{5} = -\frac{3}{5} + \frac{4}{5}\mathrm{i}$$

Evaluate the second root:
$$w_2 = \frac{-(2 + \mathrm{i})}{2 + \mathrm{i}} = -1$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Circle locus from modulus ratio |z - 4| = 2|z - 1| and powers of roots.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Expanding modulus ratio to derive Apollonius circle.

ai_rubric.observable: Squares both sides to obtain $(x - 4)^2 + y^2 = 4[(x - 1)^2 + y^2]$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding roots from intersection and calculating powers.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $x = \sqrt{3}$ into $x^2 + y^2 = 4$:
$$(\sqrt{3})^2 + y^2 = 4 \implies 3 + y^2 = 4 \implies y^2 = 1 \implies y = \pm 1$$
Roots: $z = \sqrt{3} + \mathrm{i}$ and $z = \sqrt{3} - \mathrm{i}$.

Calculate $z_1^3$ for $z_1 = \sqrt{3} + \mathrm{i}$:
$$z_1^2 = 3 + 2\sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i} - 1 = 2 + 2\sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i}$$
$$z_1^3 = (2 + 2\sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i})(\sqrt{3} + \mathrm{i}) = 2\sqrt{3} + 2\mathrm{i} + 6\mathrm{i} - 2\sqrt{3} = 8\mathrm{i}$$
$$z_1^6 = (8\mathrm{i})^2 = 64\mathrm{i}^2 = -64$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Perpendicular bisector modulus equation intersecting circle zz* = 5.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Deriving linear Cartesian equation of perpendicular bisector.

walkthrough.text:
Square both sides of $|z - 2\mathrm{i}| = |z + 4|$:
$$x^2 + (y - 2)^2 = (x + 4)^2 + y^2$$

Expand the squared terms:
$$x^2 + y^2 - 4y + 4 = x^2 + 8x + 16 + y^2$$

Cancel $x^2 + y^2$ and simplify:
$$-4y + 4 = 8x + 16 \implies 8x + 4y = -12 \implies 2x + y = -3$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up Cartesian squared moduli $x^2 + (y - 2)^2 = (x + 4)^2 + y^2$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Intersecting line locus with zz* = 5 to find complex numbers.

walkthrough.text:
Factorise the quadratic equation:
$$(x + 2)(5x + 2) = 0 \implies x = -2 \quad \text{or} \quad x = -\frac{2}{5}$$

Compute the corresponding $y$ values:
- For $x = -2$: $y = -2(-2) - 3 = 1 \implies z = -2 + \mathrm{i}$
- For $x = -\frac{2}{5}$: $y = -2(-2/5) - 3 = \frac{4}{5} - \frac{15}{5} = -\frac{11}{5} \implies z = -\frac{2}{5} - \frac{11}{5}\mathrm{i}$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Binomial expansion of z^3 + 8i = 0 in Cartesian form.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Cartesian cubic expansion and equating real and imaginary parts.

hints: Group real terms $x(x^2 - 3y^2)$ and imaginary terms $3x^2 y - y^3$.
Equate to $-8\mathrm{i} = 0 - 8\mathrm{i}$ to obtain $x(x^2 - 3y^2) = 0$ and $3x^2 y - y^3 = -8$.

walkthrough.text:
Expand $z^3 = (x + \mathrm{i}y)^3$ using binomial expansion:
$$z^3 = x^3 + 3x^2(\mathrm{i}y) + 3x(\mathrm{i}y)^2 + (\mathrm{i}y)^3$$
$$z^3 = x^3 + 3\mathrm{i}x^2 y - 3xy^2 - \mathrm{i}y^3 = (x^3 - 3xy^2) + \mathrm{i}(3x^2 y - y^3)$$

Rewrite equation as $z^3 = -8\mathrm{i}$ and equate parts:
$$\text{Real: } x^3 - 3xy^2 = x(x^2 - 3y^2) = 0$$
$$\text{Imaginary: } 3x^2 y - y^3 = -8$$

ai_rubric.observable: Groups real terms $x(x^2 - 3y^2)$ and imaginary terms $3x^2 y - y^3$.
Equates parts to obtain $x(x^2 - 3y^2) = 0$ and $3x^2 y - y^3 = -8$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding all roots from Cartesian non-linear system.

walkthrough.text:
Case 1 ($x = 0$):
$$3(0)^2 y - y^3 = -8 \implies -y^3 = -8 \implies y^3 = 8 \implies y = 2$$
$$z_1 = 2\mathrm{i}$$

Case 2 ($x^2 = 3y^2$):
$$3(3y^2)y - y^3 = -8 \implies 9y^3 - y^3 = -8 \implies 8y^3 = -8 \implies y^3 = -1 \implies y = -1$$

Find $x$ for $y = -1$:
$$x^2 = 3(-1)^2 = 3 \implies x = \pm\sqrt{3}$$
Roots: $z = 2\mathrm{i}, \sqrt{3} - \mathrm{i}, -\sqrt{3} - \mathrm{i}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Complete 4-root solution of z^2 = 4z* + 5 with real and conjugate roots.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Expanding z^2 = 4z* + 5 to derive simultaneous system.

hints: Equate real parts: $x^2 - y^2 = 4x + 5 \implies x^2 - y^2 - 4x - 5 = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Expand $z^2$ and $4z^* + 5$:
$$z^2 = (x + \mathrm{i}y)^2 = x^2 - y^2 + 2\mathrm{i}xy$$
$$4z^* + 5 = 4(x - \mathrm{i}y) + 5 = (4x + 5) - 4\mathrm{i}y$$

Equate real and imaginary components:
$$\text{Real: } x^2 - y^2 - 4x - 5 = 0$$
$$\text{Imaginary: } 2xy + 4y = 2y(x + 2) = 0$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding all 4 real and non-real roots.

walkthrough.text:
Case 1 ($y = 0$):
$$x^2 - 4x - 5 = 0 \implies (x - 5)(x + 1) = 0 \implies x = 5 \quad \text{or} \quad x = -1$$
Real roots: $z_1 = 5$ and $z_2 = -1$.

Case 2 ($x = -2$):
$$(-2)^2 - y^2 - 4(-2) - 5 = 0 \implies 4 - y^2 + 8 - 5 = 0 \implies 7 - y^2 = 0$$
$$y = \pm\sqrt{7}$$
Non-real roots: $z_3 = -2 + \sqrt{7}\,\mathrm{i}$ and $z_4 = -2 - \sqrt{7}\,\mathrm{i}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Solves Case 1 ($y = 0$) to get $x^2 - 4x - 5 = 0 \implies z = 5$ and $z = -1$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Modulus calculation and sum of squares of complex roots.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the modulus of $z_3 = -2 + \sqrt{7}\,\mathrm{i}$ and $z_4 = -2 - \sqrt{7}\,\mathrm{i}$:
$$|z_3| = |z_4| = \sqrt{(-2)^2 + (\sqrt{7})^2} = \sqrt{4 + 7} = \sqrt{11}$$

Calculate $z_3^2$ and $z_4^2$:
$$z_3^2 = (-2 + \sqrt{7}\,\mathrm{i})^2 = 4 - 4\sqrt{7}\,\mathrm{i} + 7\mathrm{i}^2 = -3 - 4\sqrt{7}\,\mathrm{i}$$
$$z_4^2 = (-2 - \sqrt{7}\,\mathrm{i})^2 = 4 + 4\sqrt{7}\,\mathrm{i} + 7\mathrm{i}^2 = -3 + 4\sqrt{7}\,\mathrm{i}$$
$$z_3^2 + z_4^2 = (-3 - 4\sqrt{7}\,\mathrm{i}) + (-3 + 4\sqrt{7}\,\mathrm{i}) = -6$$
